name: SUMPRODUCT
description: SUMPRODUCT multiplies corresponding components of one or more arrays and returns the sum of those products. It is also widely used for conditional sums and counts without array-entry.
tldr: Sums the products of corresponding array elements; great for conditional calculations.

parameters.name: array1
parameters.description: The first array or range whose elements will be multiplied and summed.

parameters.name: array2
parameters.description: Additional arrays/ranges. All arrays must have the same dimensions.

parameters.name: array3
parameters.description: Further arrays/ranges (optional). Up to 255 in modern Excel.

advancedExamples.title: Conditional sum with criteria
advancedExamples.scenario: Sum amounts in B where category in A equals "Apple".
advancedExamples.description: Use a boolean expression that SUMPRODUCT coerces to 1/0.
advancedExamples.explanation: (A1:A10="Apple") yields TRUE/FALSE; multiplying by B coerces TRUE to 1 and FALSE to 0, so only Apple rows contribute.

advancedExamples.title: Count rows meeting a condition
advancedExamples.scenario: Count how many values in A exceed 5.
advancedExamples.description: Coerce the boolean to a number and sum.
advancedExamples.explanation: (A1:A10>5) gives TRUE/FALSE; multiplying by 1 converts to 1/0, and SUMPRODUCT adds them up.

howItWorks: SUMPRODUCT takes the corresponding elements of each array, multiplies them together per position, and sums the results. With a single array it simply sums that array. Boolean criteria must be coerced to numbers (using * or --) because SUMPRODUCT does not auto-convert TRUE/FALSE.

howToSteps.name: Prepare equal-sized ranges
howToSteps.text: Ensure all arrays have the same dimensions.

howToSteps.name: Press Enter
howToSteps.text: The sum of products appears. (No array-entry needed in modern Excel.)

limitations: All array arguments must have the same dimensions, or SUMPRODUCT returns #VALUE!.
Boolean expressions must be coerced with * or --; raw TRUE/FALSE cannot be multiplied directly.
Text and empty cells within the ranges are treated as 0, which can hide data-type issues.

commonErrors.cause: Arrays have mismatched sizes, or a boolean array wasn't coerced to numbers.
commonErrors.fix: Make all ranges the same size and multiply criteria by 1 or another numeric array.

commonErrors.cause: Text/blank cells were silently treated as 0.
commonErrors.fix: Verify the ranges contain the expected numeric values.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: SUMPRODUCT works identically in Google Sheets, including the coercion-by-multiplication technique.

faq.question: Do I need to press Ctrl+Shift+Enter?
faq.answer: No. In modern Excel and Google Sheets, SUMPRODUCT handles arrays natively without special array-entry.

faq.question: Why multiply a condition by another range?
faq.answer: A condition like (A1:A10="Apple") returns TRUE/FALSE; multiplying by a numeric range coerces TRUE→1 and FALSE→0, effectively filtering the sum.

faq.question: What's the difference between SUMPRODUCT and SUMIFS?
faq.answer: SUMIFS is simpler for straightforward conditional sums, but SUMPRODUCT is more flexible (it can combine multiple AND/OR logic, weighted sums, and counts) in a single formula.
